title: CLO 2026.0 - Strap threading
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! Simply set the perforation direction to easily thread laces. Quickly create complex details such as shoelaces and corset lacing, saying goodbye to cumbersome operation steps.
transcript:
In version 2026.0, we have generously introduced a new band-aid wearing tool.  
Today, we will demonstrate how to effectively and conveniently create wearing effects for item number 1 and others.  
Previously, simulating a band-aid through eyelets was often a manual operation frequently used.  
By using the new band-aid wearing tool, you only need to select the eyelet once.  
The system can automatically plan the band-aid insertion path and direction.  
The tool can not only create a path but also generate a fully editable 2D version.  
This greatly reduces your production time and improves design efficiency.  
Next, we will use this as an example to explain the specific operation process of the tool in detail.  

The first step is to define the thread path.  
First, define the band-aid insertion path.  
From the 2D toolbar,  
select the band-aid wearing tool.  
In the 2D window,  
click the first eyelet where the band-aid is inserted or threaded through.  
Follow the expected thread path.  
Click the remaining eyelets.  
After selecting the last eyelet,  
double-click the left mouse button or press the return key to complete the path setting.  
Once the setting is complete,  
you will see the automatically generated band-aid version in the 2D window.  
You can freely edit this version.  

The second step is to select and fine-tune the settings and details.  
After completing the path setting,  
you can proceed to fine-tune the band-aid insertion path and curve to achieve the best visual effect.  
First, let's look at reversing the direction.  
After path setting is complete,  
the mouse cursor will automatically change to a reverse icon.  
At this point, click a specific eyelet.  
You can reverse the band-aid insertion direction.  
For example, change from top-to-bottom to bottom-to-top.  
The relevant adjustment will be reflected in the 3D window.  

Next, let's adjust the bend rate.  
By adjusting the bend rate slider,  
you can modify the curve of the band-aid.  
Increasing the bend rate appropriately  
can effectively prevent collisions or wear between the band-aid plate and surrounding plates,  
thereby ensuring stability in subsequent simulation.  

Next, let's review the material properties.  
The automatically generated band-aid plate  
has the physical properties of fabric.  
You can treat it like a regular clothing panel.  
Its thickness can be freely adjusted in the attribute editor,  
along with material and physical properties.  

Next, I will provide a few professional tips to improve simulation stability.  
When you need to tighten the band-aid,  
before starting the simulation,  
you can freeze all panels except the band-aid.  
Right-click on the blank area in the 3D window,  
then select simulation properties.  
Increase the bend rate value to 0.1.  
This bend rate setting helps maintain panel thickness during collisions,  
increasing the holding force.  
Raising this value ensures that when tightening the band-aid,  
it will not bounce out of the eyelet.  

Next, we can increase the length of the two ends of the band-aid  
by adding two fixed pins.  
This prevents the two ends of the band-aid from falling out of the eyelet after simulation.  
You can also adjust the width of the band-aid plate  
in the 2D window.  

Finally, before running the simulation,  
it is recommended to apply the hardening function to the band-aid plate.  
This makes the shape more solid.  

Now, let's run the simulation and tighten the band-aid.  
After tightening the band-aid plate,  
the band-aid plate will naturally fall into place.  
Replace the band-aid material.  

That’s all.  
You can use this tool to create more diversified band-aid effects.  

Next, I will show you three different band-aid effects.  
In this example, I used  
two fixed pins.  
The first effect is to create a band-aid segment.  
This accelerates the band-aid simulation.  
The second band-aid effect you can create is  
to check if the band-aid is tight enough.  

Here we go.  
From now on, even when facing the most complex binding structures, you only need to simply click and tweak the parameters a few times, and you can easily fix it.  
We look forward to your use of this efficient new function to create more amazing 3D works.

chunks.content: ## Introduction to the Band-Aid Wearing Tool in CLO 2026.0 This section introduces the new band-aid wearing tool in CLO 2026.0, designed to simplify and automate the process of creating band-aid style wearing effects on garments, particularly for eyelet threading. The tool enhances design efficiency by automatically planning insertion paths and generating editable 2D band-aid versions. - The band-aid wearing tool automates creating band-aid effects through eyelets. - It requires selecting eyelets once, after which the system generates the insertion path. - Produces a fully editable 2D band-aid version. - Significantly reduces production time and improves design workflows. ## Defining the Band-Aid Thread Path This section explains how to define and set the band-aid insertion path using the band-aid wearing tool in the 2D window of CLO. ### Procedure: 1. Open the 2D toolbar and select the band-aid wearing tool. 2. In the 2D window, click the first eyelet where the band-aid will be inserted. 3. Follow the expected thread path by clicking subsequent eyelets in order. 4. After selecting the final eyelet, double-click or press the return key to complete the path. 5. The software automatically generates the band-aid version in the 2D window, which is fully editable. ## Fine-Tuning Band-Aid Path and Visual Effects This section covers adjusting the band-aid insertion path and its visual properties to enhance realism and simulation stability. ### Key Adjustments: - **Reversing Direction:** After setting the path, the cursor changes to a reverse icon. Clicking a specific eyelet reverses the insertion direction (e.g., top-to-bottom to bottom-to-top), with changes reflected in the 3D window. - **Adjusting Bend Rate:** Use the bend rate slider to modify the curvature of the band-aid. Increasing the bend rate helps prevent collisions between the band-aid plate and adjacent panels, improving simulation stability. - **Material Properties:** The generated band-aid plate has fabric physical properties and can be treated like a regular clothing panel. Thickness, material, and physical properties are adjustable in the attribute editor. ## Professional Tips for Simulation Stability This section provides expert recommendations to ensure effective and stable band-aid simulations. ### Tips: - **Freezing Panels:** Before simulation, freeze all panels except the band-aid by right-clicking on the blank area in the 3D window and selecting simulation properties. - **Increasing Bend Rate:** Set the bend rate value to 0.1 to maintain panel thickness during collisions. This increases the holding force, preventing the band-aid from bouncing out of eyelets when tightened. - **Adding Fixed Pins:** Add two fixed pins at the ends of the band-aid to extend its length, preventing the ends from falling out of eyelets after simulation. - **Adjusting Width:** Modify the band-aid plate width in the 2D window to better fit design requirements. - **Applying Hardening:** Use the hardening function on the band-aid plate before running simulation to make the shape more solid and maintain its structure during tightening. ## Running Simulation and Band-Aid Tightening This section describes the final simulation process where the band-aid is tightened and positioned naturally.
